title: Adobe OAuth Web App client secret as a form parameter or as a decoded clientId:clientSecret pair
summary: A client_secret form parameter in an authorization-code token request of a Web App credential, and the decoded clientId:clientSecret text that the Basic header encodes.
rationale: Adobe's sample OpenID configuration lists client_secret_basic and client_secret_post, but the parameter tables and request examples of the OAuth Web App credential document only the Basic Authorization header (contract claim web-app-metadata-lists-two-auth-methods), so a client_secret form parameter is not a documented Web App carrier, unlike the Server-to-Server and Enterprise carriers. The decoded clientId:clientSecret text is the input of the header construction; whether a decoded header is in scope is the contract's open question basic-header-is-derived-form. No outcome is asserted for either.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Whether a client_secret form parameter in a Web App token request, and the decoded clientId:clientSecret text, carry the Web App client secret is not stated by any Adobe page. Settled by an Adobe page documenting the Web App client_secret_post form, or a downstream decision on decoded headers recorded as a separate policy.

sources.supports: The authorization parameter is required for confidential clients as Authorization: Basic Base64(clientId:clientSecret) on the access-token and refresh requests (the request example for the OAuth Web App credential carries only the Authorization header and the code or refresh_token); the revocation request takes the same header for OAuth Web and OAuth WebApp credentials; client_id is required for public clients.
sources.locator: sections "Fetching Access tokens", "Refreshing Access tokens" and "Token revocation", parameter tables and Web App request examples

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. No outcome is asserted. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
